chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Take the wealth of the al-Nasib (rival) wherever you find it, and pay the khums to us."

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: The rival (al-Nasib), specifically referring to the Umayyads in Shia tradition.
key_terms.الْخُمُسَ: The one-fifth tax, a specific religious levy in Shia jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking the wealth of the al-Nasib and paying khums?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Imam’s right to seize the wealth of the *al-Nasib* (specifically the Umayyads and their followers) as a form of divine retribution and political claim. It links this seizure directly to the obligation of paying *khums* (one-fifth) to the Imam, reinforcing the concept of *khums* not merely as a tax but as a mechanism of legitimizing Imamate authority over rival factions. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the distribution of war booty and specific tributes from enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt.
